case_name: Faridabad Gas Power Project, Ntpc Ltd., Etc. v Om Prakash & Ors., Etc.
petitioner: Faridabad Gas Power Project, Ntpc Ltd., Etc
facts: The State of Haryana issued Notification dated 16.08.1995 u/s.4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 for acquisition of a track of 319.31 acres of lands in five villages...

The Land Acquisition Collector, Faridabad awarded compensation at the rate of Rs.2,50,000/- per acre for Chahi land, i.e. about Rs.52/- per sq. yard and Rs.2,00,000/- per acre, i.e. Rs.42/- per sq. yard for Banjar Kadim and Gair Mumkin lands...
The claimants preferred reference applications u/s.18 of the Act.

Before the reference court (Additional District Judge, Faridabad), the parties led evidence and raised mainly the following two issues:-(i) What was the market price of the acquired land on the date of publication of notification u/s.4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894?
(ii) Whether the petitioners are estopped from filing the petition by their acts and conduct?
issues: What was the market price of the acquired land on the date of publication of notification u/s.4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894?
Whether the petitioners are estopped from filing the petition by their acts and conduct?
petitioner_arguments: The reference court as well as the High Court, both have wrongly ignored the said transactions from consideration merely on the grounds that the instances of sale portions of the land were made about two years before the Notification issued u/s.4(1) of the Act in the present cases and approximately one year after the acquisition of the land.

Reference to the sale deed dated 23.06.1994 (Exhibit R6) has been made by the learned counsel vide which Raghbir and Ram Lal had sold land measuring 1 Kanal and 10 Marlas situated in village Mujheri to Manoj Goyal for a consideration of Rs.40,000/- [about Rs.44.40 per sq. yard].

Copy of another sale deed dated 30.06.1993 (Exhibit R5) vide which Smt. Kamla had sold land measuring 1 Kanal 11 Marlas in village Mujheri in favour of Haria for a sum of Rs.39,000/- [about Rs.41.58 per sq. yard] was also relied on by Mr. Dhingra.
respondent_arguments: The acquired land is situated in different villages far away from the urban areas of Faridabad - Ballabgarh towns and did not possess any potentiality other than being agricultural land.
The claimants had accepted the compensation without protest; that the acquired land has no potential value for residential or commercial purposes.
court_reasoning: We have heard the learned counsel for all the parties. Mr. S.K. Dhingra, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the NTPC, contended that sale deeds produced by the appellants ought to have been accepted as a piece of best evidence for determining the market value of the land in question...
holding: The High Court by its judgment dated 29.05.2004 dismissed all the appeals and thereby confirmed the award made by the reference court.
